method: Read-only SSH: container status, recent service logs, PostgreSQL read-only transactions, public HTTPS readiness, and local source inspection.

findings.finding: Both recent failed chats consumed the full eight-call tool budget. This is the chat execution budget, distinct from source-fetch request quotas.
findings.evidence: agent_runs rows and persisted failed run_events

findings.finding: The agent keeps offering tools at the limit and throws on an additional requested call. It has no budget-aware final-answer phase.
The chat page maps every nonempty errorCode to the same instruction to check materials or retry; it does not explain this failure.
Chat failures are persisted via callbacks, but AgentRuntime's rejection handler does not log their code or run ID. HTTP 200 callbacks and healthy containers therefore do not prove successful chats.

otherObservedState.mcpGet405: The API deliberately returns 405 for authenticated GET /mcp; this is also seen alongside successful chats and does not establish their failure cause.

limitations: Individual tool names and arguments are not retained in the inspected runtime logs, so this investigation does not identify which exact tool sequence consumed the budget.
The same error code also covers excessive serialized model input; full budget consumption is confirmed, but the exact throwing branch cannot be proven from these stored records alone.
No new model inference, source request, production restart, configuration change, or code deployment was performed.
This is a diagnosis, not a completed fix or production acceptance.
